vision: A distributable library of AI coding assistant rules, skills, hooks, and a file-based harness for Cursor and Claude Code. THE HARNESS IS: a durable, file-system task system that keeps AI agents honest across sessions. It solves five problems the owner identified: (1) repository scope — vision, direction, trade-offs in state.json; (2) task definition — discrete tasks with type and scope; (3) task grouping — flat tasks[] array filtered by status at read time; (4) task status tracking — lifecycle enum + append-only breadcrumbs.jsonl for session recovery; (5) acceptance criteria — contract.json with binary-testable criteria negotiated before implementation. For whom: teams using Cursor/Claude Code on non-trivial multi-file work who need agents to stop self-grading and stop losing context between sessions. Why each component exists: state.json = scope + backlog; contract.json = definition of done; breadcrumbs = audit trail; planner subagent = decompose vague requests; evaluator subagent = adversarial QA separate from builder context; hooks (lean) = enforce contract-before-code structurally; eval pipeline = regression test that agents follow the workflow. HONEST ASSESSMENT: the core five-problem harness is sound and ~40 lines of JSON + rules. Everything layered on top — negotiations/ JSON schemas, 11 hooks (full profile), metrics dashboard, 41 scenario evals with 5 judge tiers, multi-agent orchestration, UI dashboard — has grown organically and now obscures the value proposition. 47 verified tasks prove the core works; 13 pending tasks are mostly eval-tooling bugs and nice-to-haves, not harness failures. RESEARCH TRACK (spike-research-agents): Produce publication-grade landscape analysis of AI agent configuration — rules, skills, agentic loops, subagents, prompts, system prompts — answering what average users do vs. what advanced practitioners do, with an honest evidence-based positioning of this repo and a transferable maturity model (ACAM) others can use to assess their own setups.
direction: DUAL TRACK (2026-06-11): (A) EVAL TOOLING — spike-eval-research VERIFIED; remaining: feat-14a (LLM judge calibration), feat-16 (rule ablation), chore-skill-scenarios, gap-14 session boundary, gap-18 skip-harness auth, chore-archive-review. Architecture unchanged: structural deny for critical steps, advisory for quality signals. (B) RESEARCH — spike-research-agents (REVISED): 7 phases across 4 consolidated dimensions (Configuration, Workflows, Multi-agent, Interaction) + data collection phase + synthesis. ACAM simplified to 3 levels (Basic/Intermediate/Advanced). Target: practitioner reference guide suitable for conference talk or blog series — not academic paper. Includes GitHub .cursorrules scraping and comparable setup analysis (Aider, SWE-agent, Devin). Research is analysis-only — no code. Honest positioning required; cite repo artifacts + external data, not aspirations.

trade_offs.reasoning: Hooks and agents iterate one list today; grouped buckets duplicate items and drift. harness-context.sh can filter by status at read time.
Eight lean hooks, harness_lint.py, and 20 eval scenarios already encode this lifecycle. done conflates verified and committed; doing conflates building and evaluating.

trade_offs.decision: Explicit type enum on every task
trade_offs.alternative: Infer type from id prefix only (feat-/gap-/spike-)
trade_offs.reasoning: Id prefixes are convention not validation; explicit type enables lint enforcement and clearer planner output.
22+ eval scenario seeds and 6 shell hooks read features today; alias prevents eval regression during phased rollout.
Preserves audit trail; metrics exclude cancelled from backlog counts.

trade_offs.alternative: Keep symlinks tracked, gitignore only transient files
trade_offs.reasoning: Matches how consumer projects treat IDE config; library/cursor/ is the distributable artifact
spec.md was read once (plan gate) then became stale. Single file eliminates drift by design.

trade_offs.alternative: Build evaluator chaining and parallel evaluators
trade_offs.reasoning: Manual /evaluator launch works. Orchestration adds complexity for a problem (evaluator doesn't run) already solved by chain-evaluator.sh hook and rules. No user demand.
state.json and breadcrumbs are human-readable JSON. Dashboard solves a problem that doesn't exist yet. metrics.json is broken anyway (gap-21).

trade_offs.decision: Defer feat-14 LLM-as-judge until after schema consolidation
trade_offs.alternative: Build LLM judge now to fix UNCERTAIN verdicts
trade_offs.reasoning: 89.8% mean is acceptable. Many UNCERTAIN/FAIL are judge bugs (gap-20 harness_level placement, gap-19 heuristics), not agent failures. Fix tooling before adding LLM cost.
Eval accuracy issues are symptoms of schema drift and inconsistent harness_level placement across 41 scenarios. Consolidation fixes root cause.

trade_offs.decision: Keep lean hook profile as default; demote full profile
trade_offs.reasoning: Lean (4 hooks) enforces the five-problem core. Full profile adds dedup-server, context-health, evaluator-guard, harness-gate LLM routing — valuable for this repo's dogfooding, optional for consumers.

trade_offs.alternative: Enforce structured negotiation JSON per HARNESS_STANDARD.md
trade_offs.reasoning: negotiations/ directory is rarely populated in practice. Breadcrumbs with type=negotiate capture the same signal with less schema burden. HARNESS_STANDARD over-specifies this artifact.

trade_offs.decision: Decompose spike-eval-research into 6 sequential research phases
trade_offs.reasoning: Four distinct eval dimensions (rules, skills, trajectory, LLM judge) plus baseline inventory and synthesis need focused research passes. Sequential phases produce partial notes that roll into one spike doc without scope creep into implementation.

trade_offs.decision: Consolidate 6 research dimensions into 4 (Configuration, Workflows, Multi-agent, Interaction) + add data collection phase
trade_offs.alternative: Keep 6 separate dimensions (rules, skills, loops, subagents, prompts, system prompts)
trade_offs.reasoning: Builder review identified heavy overlap: rules ARE system prompts; prompts and system prompts are one dimension with sub-layers; skills define workflows within loops. 4 dimensions allow deeper analysis per phase. Separate data collection phase (GitHub scraping, comparable setups) prevents the spike from being pure desk-research opinion.

5-level maturity models (CMMI-style) are notorious for hair-splitting between adjacent levels. 3 levels with clear behavioral markers per dimension are more practical and adoptable. Each level has observable signals, not abstract capability descriptions.

trade_offs.decision: Target: practitioner reference guide, not academic paper
trade_offs.alternative: Aim for academic publication (requires IRB, statistical framework, peer review)
trade_offs.reasoning: The plan has zero empirical data collection methodology, no IRB, no statistical framework. Most impactful AI tooling content is practitioner-oriented. Blog series + conference talk format reaches the target audience directly. Academic rigor can come later with feat-16 ablation data.

trade_offs.decision: Research outputs live in .harness/docs/research/ not docs/
trade_offs.alternative: Publish directly to docs/ for consumer visibility
trade_offs.reasoning: Research is in-progress spike artifacts with bibliography and scorecard JSON; docs/ is consumer-facing standards. Move to docs/ only after synthesis phase validates ACAM and owner approves publication.

tasks.name: Research: AI agent configuration landscape — normie vs advanced, rules-skills positioning

tasks.details:
KEY QUESTION: What do average users do vs. what advanced practitioners do in AI agent configuration — and where does rules-skills honestly sit?

TARGET: Practitioner reference guide — rigorous enough for a conference talk or multi-part blog series. NOT an academic paper (no IRB, no statistical framework). The audience is teams adopting AI coding assistants who want to know what 'good' looks like.

4 CONSOLIDATED DIMENSIONS (not 6 — builder review identified heavy overlap):

| Dimension | Covers | Why consolidated |
|-----------|--------|------------------|
| Configuration | Rules + system prompts + .cursorrules + platform config layers | Rules ARE user-level system prompts; platform vs user config is a sub-layer, not separate dimension |
| Workflows | Skills + agentic loops + lifecycle enforcement + hooks | Skills define workflows within the loop; separating them creates artificial boundary |
| Multi-agent | Subagents + orchestration + context isolation + role separation | Natural grouping — how agents collaborate |
| Interaction | User prompts + meta-prompts + prompt coaching + structured input | How humans communicate intent to agents |

ACAM MATURITY MODEL — 3 levels (not 5):

| Level | Name | Observable signal |
|-------|------|-------------------|
| Basic | Default/ad-hoc | Zero or copy-pasted config, no verification, single-shot prompts |
| Intermediate | Structured/intentional | Versioned rules, defined workflows, role separation, some testing |
| Advanced | Measured/enforced | Structural enforcement, eval regression suites, data-driven iteration, quantitative evidence of effectiveness |

Why 3 not 5: CMMI-style 5-level models invite hair-splitting. 3 levels with clear behavioral markers are more practical and adoptable.

PHASES (7 phases, ~2-3h each, sequential):

Phase 1 — Methodology + Repo Inventory
- Define operational terms (Basic/Intermediate/Advanced) with observable signals per dimension
- Build annotated bibliography template; seed with Anthropic agent guides, OpenAI best practices, Cursor docs, SWE-agent/ReAct papers, community repos
- §0 repo inventory: 16 rules, 14 skills, 28 eval scenarios, lean+full hook profiles, 3-role subagent model, sync system
- Define data collection targets for Phase 2
- Output: .harness/docs/research/phase-1-methodology.md + bibliography.md

Phase 2 — Data Collection (NEW — external evidence)
- Scrape GitHub for .cursorrules / .cursor/rules/ patterns: count files, avg size, common patterns, token budgets
- Analyze community repos: awesome-cursorrules, cursor-tools, published rule sets
- Deep-dive 5 comparable setups: (1) Aider config/conventions, (2) SWE-agent tooling, (3) Devin-like agent architectures, (4) Claude Code CLAUDE.md patterns, (5) Windsurf/Copilot config
- Interview/survey proxy: mine Reddit r/cursor, Cursor forum, Discord for user behavior patterns
- Classify findings into Basic/Intermediate/Advanced per dimension
- Output: .harness/docs/research/phase-2-data-collection.md + raw-data/ folder

Phase 3 — Configuration (rules + system prompts + platform layers)
- Literature: always-on constraints, .mdc/.cursorrules formats, token budget trade-offs, rule conflicts, platform system prompt layering
- Basic: default IDE settings, zero rules, or single monolithic .cursorrules
- Intermediate: multiple rules with globs, sizing standards, separate concerns
- Advanced: versioned rule libraries, ablation testing, measured effectiveness, structural loading strategies
- rules-skills evidence: library/cursor/rules/ (16 files), docs/RULES_STANDARD.md, alwaysApply ~2000 token budget, glob-scoped rules
- Honest gaps: no rule effectiveness metrics (feat-16 pending), progress_tracking + planning_discipline overlap, no prompt injection defense
- Cross-reference Phase 2 data: how does our 16-rule corpus compare to GitHub median?
- Output: .harness/docs/research/phase-3-configuration.md

Phase 4 — Workflows (skills + agentic loops + lifecycle enforcement)
- Literature: SKILL.md format, ReAct loops, plan-execute-verify, CI-gated agent workflows, contract-first development, hook enforcement
- Basic: no skills, single-shot prompts, agent self-grades, no verification
- Intermediate: saved workflows/skills, explicit loop (plan→build→verify), manual checkpoints
- Advanced: structural enforcement (hooks deny bad actions), eval regression suites, contract negotiation, measured skill effectiveness
- rules-skills evidence: 14 skills + SKILLS_STANDARD, adversarial harness lifecycle, contract-gate + verify-harness hooks, 28 eval scenarios
- Honest gaps: zero skill_activation eval coverage (chore-skill-scenarios pending), verify-harness trusts contract.verified, session boundary 33% (gap-14)
- Output: .harness/docs/research/phase-4-workflows.md

Phase 5 — Multi-agent (subagents + orchestration + context isolation)
- Literature: task decomposition, adversarial QA, AutoGen, CrewAI, Claude subagents, Cursor /commands and Task tool
- Basic: single agent, builder self-reviews, no role separation
- Intermediate: dedicated planner/evaluator roles, manual handoffs, context isolation
- Advanced: programmatic orchestration, parallel evaluation, auto-routing, measured inter-agent effectiveness
- rules-skills evidence: planner/builder/evaluator model, chain-evaluator.sh, evaluator-guard hook
- Honest gaps: manual /planner + /evaluator launches (feat-13 cancelled = no auto-orchestration), negotiations/ rarely used, no parallel evaluators
- Output: .harness/docs/research/phase-5-multi-agent.md

Phase 6 — Interaction (user prompts + meta-prompts + prompt coaching)
- Literature: prompt engineering evolution, structured prompting, meta-prompts for roles, prompt injection, few-shot/chain-of-thought in agent context
- Basic: vague one-liners ('fix this'), no structure, no context management
- Intermediate: structured prompts (context/constraints/verification), thread hygiene, scoping requests
- Advanced: meta-prompts in subagent definitions, prompt coaching rules, measured prompt effectiveness, versioned prompt libraries
- rules-skills evidence: prompt_coaching.mdc, subagent role definitions, planning_discipline.mdc (thread hygiene), critical_thinking.mdc
- Honest gaps: no prompt versioning, no prompt A/B testing separate from rule ablation, no user interaction analytics
- Output: .harness/docs/research/phase-6-interaction.md

Phase 7 — Synthesis + ACAM + Publication
- Consolidate phases 3-6 into cross-dimension taxonomy
- Build ACAM model: 4 dimensions × 3 levels with observable criteria per cell, assessment worksheet
- Score rules-skills per dimension with evidence paths + Phase 2 comparative data
- Identify: genuinely advanced (structural contract-gate, eval regression), mid-tier (skills without activation eval), over-engineered (full hook profile, cancelled features)
- Red-team: 3 ways the repo is NOT advanced despite appearing sophisticated
- Draft publication: talk abstract + 4-part blog series outline + 'assess your setup' worksheet
- Output: .harness/docs/research/acam-maturity-model.md + rules-skills-scorecard.json + .harness/docs/spike-research-agents.md

DELIVERABLES:
1. bibliography.md — annotated source corpus (min 30 sources)
2. phase-{1-7}-*.md — per-phase analysis notes (7 files)
3. acam-maturity-model.md — transferable 4×3 framework + assessment worksheet
4. rules-skills-scorecard.json — per-dimension score + evidence[] + gaps[] + frontier_comparison
5. spike-research-agents.md — master synthesis (self-contained)
6. Publication appendix — talk abstract + blog series TOC

SELF-ASSESSMENT RULES:
- Every score cites ≥2 repo artifacts as evidence
- Every gap references a pending task, eval score, or explicit absence
- Advanced requires quantitative evidence — no aspirational Advanced without data
- Baselines defined from Phase 2 data (GitHub scraping, community analysis), not stereotypes
- Frontier cites external exemplars (named projects, papers, vendor guides)
- Red-team pass: 3 ways the repo is NOT advanced despite sophistication
- One-paragraph honest positioning summary

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
- All 7 phase docs exist with bibliography cross-refs
- ACAM has filled row for rules-skills in every dimension
- Phase 2 data collection produced quantitative baselines (not just opinion)
- Master synthesis is self-contained (readable without phase docs)
- ACAM worksheet copyable to another repo, scorable in 30 minutes

BIAS CORRECTIONS (binding, from Phase 1 self-audit — documented in phase-1-methodology.md §9):
- BC1: Each phase must cite ≥3 external sources NOT referenced in any prior repo doc
- BC2: Phase 2 bibliography must include ≥2 sources arguing AGAINST complex agent config (simplicity-first, over-engineering warnings)
- BC3: ACAM criteria must be validated against external vocabulary in Phase 7, not our own jargon
- BC4: Phase 2 must add Devin + ≥1 setup that may be MORE advanced than rules-skills
- BC5: Normie baseline must come from Phase 2 GitHub data, not stereotypes — if median user has scoped .mdc, Intermediate is the new normal
- BC6: Final self-assessment (Phase 7) = Intermediate WITHOUT asterisks or hedging. Built ≠ proved.
